# Python API reference

<!-- generated by docs/gen_reference.py from the code: do not edit by hand -->

Everything below is importable as shown. `from vidlabel import ...` gives the names listed in `vidlabel.__all__`; the rest live in the module named in each heading. Concepts and examples are in the other pages (start with [concepts](concepts.md) and [getting started](getting-started.md)).

## Datasets

### `Dataset`

```python
Dataset(path: str | Path)
```

A vidlabel dataset: a folder of plain files (see docs/SPEC.md). Make one with `Dataset.create(path)`, open one with
`Dataset.open(path)`. There is no server and no lock: one writer per video at a time.

#### `Dataset.add_annotations`

```python
add_annotations(
    rows: Iterable[Mapping[str, Any]],
    video_id: str | None = None,
    *,
    create_labels: bool = False,
    validate: bool = True,
    coords: str = 'source',
) -> list[int]
```

Append annotations. Rows are dicts using the column names (plus `box=(x0,y0,x1,y1)` shorthand).

A mask row may pass `mask=<bool ndarray HxW>`; it is encoded and its box filled in automatically.
Returns the new annotation ids. Raises ValidationError (writing nothing) if any row is invalid.

coords="source" (default): boxes/masks are in full source-video pixels.
coords="view": boxes/masks are in the pixels of the row's `view_id` (the crop as the pipeline saw it) and are
converted to source coordinates here (offset, plus scaling if the view has `output_size`). Masks must be
boolean arrays the size of the view region or of its `output_size`.

#### `Dataset.add_labels`

```python
add_labels(labels: Iterable[str | Label | Mapping]) -> list[str]
```

Add labels to the shared vocabulary (existing names are left alone). Returns the names actually added.

#### `Dataset.add_video`

```python
add_video(
    meta: VideoMetadata | Mapping[str, Any],
    exist_ok: bool = False,
    *,
    frame_index: FrameIndex | None = None,
) -> VideoMetadata
```

Register a video from a VideoMetadata (or a dict of its fields), e.g. from `probe_video`. The video file itself
is never copied. Raises FileExistsError if the id exists, unless `exist_ok=True` (which replaces the metadata).

`frame_index` (from `probe_frame_index`) is stored next to the metadata; see `set_frame_index`.

#### `Dataset.add_view`

```python
add_view(view: View | Mapping[str, Any], exist_ok: bool = False) -> View
```

Define a named crop and/or frame range of a registered video (see docs/views.md). The region must fit inside the
video, `frame_range` inside its length, and `allowed_labels` must already be in the vocabulary.

#### `Dataset.annotations`

```python
annotations(
    video_id: str | None = None,
    *,
    kind: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    label: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    origin: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    status: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    view_id: str | Sequence[str | None] | None = None,
    frames: tuple[int, int] | None = None,
    columns: Sequence[str] | None = None,
) -> pa.Table
```

Query annotations as a pyarrow Table. `frames=(a, b)` keeps annotations overlapping [a, b] inclusive.

`view_id` keeps rows labelled in that view (or any of several). Include None in a list to also (or only)
get whole-frame rows that have no view, e.g. `view_id=[None]`.

#### `Dataset.build`

```python
build(**kwargs)
```

Compile a training release: `build(**kwargs)` forwards to `vidlabel.build.build` and returns `(Release, path)`.

#### `Dataset.create`

```python
create(path: str | Path, exist_ok: bool = False) -> 'Dataset'
```

Make an empty dataset folder. Raises FileExistsError if one is already there, unless `exist_ok=True`.

#### `Dataset.delete_annotations`

```python
delete_annotations(video_id: str, annotation_ids: Iterable[int]) -> int
```

Remove annotations of one video by id. Returns how many rows were removed.

#### `Dataset.frame_index`

```python
frame_index(video_id: str) -> FrameIndex | None
```

The stored frame index of a video (timestamps and keyframes), or None if it has none.

#### `Dataset.manifest` (property)

The parsed manifest.json: spec version, video ids and view ids.

#### `Dataset.open`

```python
open(path: str | Path) -> 'Dataset'
```

Open an existing dataset. Raises FileNotFoundError if the folder is not a vidlabel dataset.

#### `Dataset.resolve_video_path`

```python
resolve_video_path(video_id: str, roots: Sequence[str | Path] = ()) -> Path | None
```

Find the video file: try each recorded source, then search `roots` for the same file name.

#### `Dataset.set_frame_index`

```python
set_frame_index(video_id: str, index: FrameIndex) -> None
```

Store (or replace) the frame index of a registered video. Raises ValueError if it has a different number of
frames than the metadata says, or was made from a different file (hash mismatch).

#### `Dataset.stats`

```python
stats() -> dict[str, Any]
```

Counts for `vidlabel info`: totals, and breakdowns by kind, label, origin, status and view, plus one entry per video.

#### `Dataset.update_annotations`

```python
update_annotations(video_id: str, annotation_ids: Iterable[int], **values: Any) -> int
```

Set columns (e.g. status='approved', label='x') on the given annotations. Returns rows changed.

#### `Dataset.validate`

```python
validate(deep: bool = False) -> list[Issue]
```

Check the whole dataset against the spec and return a list of Issues (empty = valid). Never raises for bad data.
`deep=True` also decodes every mask and checks it against its box and the frame size.

#### `Dataset.video`

```python
video(video_id: str) -> VideoMetadata
```

Metadata of one registered video. Raises KeyError for an unknown id.

#### `Dataset.video_ids`

```python
video_ids() -> list[str]
```

Ids of all registered videos, sorted.

#### `Dataset.view`

```python
view(view_id: str) -> View
```

One view definition. Raises KeyError for an unknown id.

#### `Dataset.view_ids`

```python
view_ids() -> list[str]
```

Ids of all views, sorted.

#### `Dataset.vocab` (property)

The parsed vocab.json: the one shared label list.

## Releases (compiled training tables)

### `vidlabel.build.build`

```python
build(
    ds: Dataset,
    *,
    statuses: Sequence[str] = ('unreviewed', 'approved'),
    origins: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    kinds: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    video_ids: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    view_ids: Sequence[str | None] | None = None,
    row_group_size: int = 20000,
    check: bool = True,
) -> tuple[Release, Path]
```

Write compiled/<release_id>/{annotations.parquet, vocab.json, release.json}. Rejected annotations are excluded by default.

vocab.json is a snapshot of the label vocabulary, so class indices derived from a pinned release cannot change when
labels are added to the dataset later.

The release id is the hash of the file contents: same data and filters give the same id, so a training run can
record it and later reproduce exactly the same table.

### `vidlabel.build.Compiled`

```python
vidlabel.build.Compiled(path: str | Path)
```

Reader for a compiled release. Fast clip lookups use Parquet row-group statistics (the table is sorted).

#### `vidlabel.build.Compiled.clip`

```python
clip(
    video_id: str,
    start: int,
    end: int,
    columns: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    view_id: str | None = None,
) -> pa.Table
```

Annotations of one video overlapping frames [start, end] inclusive, reading only the row groups that can match.

`view_id` additionally keeps only rows labelled in that view.

#### `vidlabel.build.Compiled.read`

```python
read(columns: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> pa.Table
```

The whole release table (or only `columns`) as a pyarrow Table, sorted by video, start frame and annotation id.

#### `vidlabel.build.Compiled.release_id` (property)

The release id, e.g. `r3fa91c0b2d44`: derived from the table's contents.

#### `vidlabel.build.Compiled.row_groups_for`

```python
row_groups_for(video_id: str, start: int, end: int) -> list[int]
```

Indices of the Parquet row groups that can contain annotations of `video_id` overlapping frames [start, end].

#### `vidlabel.build.Compiled.vocab` (property)

The label vocabulary as it was when this release was built (None for releases made before it was saved).

## Training samples

### `vidlabel.samples.FrameSamples`

```python
vidlabel.samples.FrameSamples(
    ds: Dataset,
    *,
    release: str | None = 'latest',
    view_id: str | None = None,
    videos: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    kinds: Sequence[str] = ('box', 'mask'),
    labels: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    origins: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    min_confidence: float | None = None,
    frames: str = 'annotated',
    stride: int = 1,
    with_masks: bool = False,
    box_format: str = 'xyxy',
    normalized: bool = False,
    label_offset: int = 0,
    roots: Sequence[str | Path] = (),
    cache: FrameCache | str | Path | None = None,
)
```

Which frames to train on, and what the targets for each are. Build it once, then read samples by (video, frame).

Parameters (all keyword-only except `ds`):

- `release`: `"latest"`, a release id such as `"r3fa91c0b2d44"` (pinned: the same rows and class indices every time), or
  `None` to read the live annotations (unreviewed and approved), which can change between runs.
- `view_id`: train on that view's crop with only that view's annotations. `None`: full frames, all annotations.
- `videos`: restrict to these video ids (default: all).
- `kinds`: which kinds define the samples and targets, from `"box"`, `"mask"`, `"marker"`. Markers always fill
  `frame_labels`; add `"marker"` to also sample frames that only have a marker.
- `labels`: keep only these labels; class indices then follow this order (default: the vocabulary's order).
- `origins`: keep only rows with these origins, e.g. `["human"]`.
- `min_confidence`: drop rows whose confidence is below this (rows with no confidence are kept).
- `frames`: `"annotated"` (frames with a selected annotation) or `"all"` (every frame).
- `stride`: keep every Nth frame of that list.
- `with_masks`: decode masks into the sample (`masks`, aligned with `boxes`).
- `box_format`: `"xyxy"`, `"xywh"` or `"cxcywh"`; `normalized=True` gives fractions of the image size.
- `label_offset`: added to class indices (e.g. `1` for detectors that reserve 0 for background).
- `roots`: folders to search for videos whose recorded path is stale.
- `cache`: a `FrameCache` (or the folder of one made by `vidlabel cache`). Frames it holds are read as image files
  instead of decoded from video; anything missing falls back to the video. See docs/training.md.

See docs/training.md for what a sample contains.

#### `vidlabel.samples.FrameSamples.describe`

```python
describe() -> dict
```

What to log next to a training run so it can be reproduced.

#### `vidlabel.samples.FrameSamples.frames_of`

```python
frames_of(video_id: str) -> list[int]
```

The frame numbers sampled from one video, in order.

#### `vidlabel.samples.FrameSamples.reader`

```python
reader(video_id: str)
```

A reader for one video (`read(frame)`, `read_many(frames)`, `close()`), already set up with this object's view.
It uses the video's frame index when it has one, and the frame cache if there is one that matches the video.
Close it when done (or use `with`).

#### `vidlabel.samples.FrameSamples.sample`

```python
sample(video_id: str, frame: int, image: np.ndarray) -> dict
```

The full sample for a frame whose pixels you already have.

#### `vidlabel.samples.FrameSamples.targets`

```python
targets(video_id: str, frame: int, image_size: tuple[int, int]) -> dict
```

Boxes, labels, masks and frame labels for one frame. `image_size` is (width, height) of the image returned.

#### `vidlabel.samples.FrameSamples.video_ids`

```python
video_ids() -> list[str]
```

Videos that contribute at least one sample.

#### `vidlabel.samples.FrameSamples.video_path`

```python
video_path(video_id: str) -> Path
```

Where the video file is on this machine (recorded paths first, then `roots`). Raises FileNotFoundError.

### PyTorch (`vidlabel.torch_data`, needs `vidlabel[torch]`)

`VideoStream` and `VideoFrames` are documented in [training](training.md); `collate_frames(batch)` batches samples (stacking images that share a size) and `to_tensors(sample)` converts a NumPy sample to tensors (image as uint8 CHW).

## Frames and previews (need OpenCV: `vidlabel[video]`)

### `vidlabel.frames.read_frames`

```python
read_frames(
    path: str | Path,
    frame_indices: Iterable[int],
    meta: VideoMetadata,
    *,
    view: View | None = None,
) -> Iterator[tuple[int, np.ndarray]]
```

Yield (frame_index, RGB frame) for each requested index, in increasing order.

Raises ValueError if the file's frame size does not match `meta` (wrong or re-encoded file) and IndexError if a
requested frame is past the end of the video.

### `vidlabel.frames.read_frame`

```python
read_frame(
    path: str | Path,
    index: int,
    meta: VideoMetadata,
    *,
    view: View | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray
```

One frame, RGB, displayed orientation. Decodes from the start of the video: use `read_frames` or `FrameReader` for many.

### `vidlabel.frames.check_video`

```python
check_video(path: str | Path, meta: VideoMetadata, *, verify_hash: bool = False) -> list[str]
```

Compare a video file with the metadata registered for it. Returns a list of problems (empty = consistent).

### `vidlabel.frames.crop_to_view`

```python
crop_to_view(frame: np.ndarray, view: View | None) -> np.ndarray
```

Crop a displayed-orientation frame to a view's region and resize to its output_size (if any).

### `vidlabel.frames.seek_mismatches`

```python
seek_mismatches(
    path: str | Path,
    meta: VideoMetadata,
    positions: Iterable[int],
    index: FrameIndex | None = None,
) -> list[int]
```

Frames at `positions` for which seeking does NOT return exactly what sequential decoding returns.

Empty means seeking is frame-exact at those positions. OpenCV's seek is exact for ordinary constant-frame-rate
files but can land a few frames off on variable-frame-rate video or odd containers, which would silently misalign
every box, so without an index seeking is only used after this check (see `FrameReader`). With `index`, the reader
under test is the indexed one.

### `vidlabel.frames.FrameReader`

```python
vidlabel.frames.FrameReader(
    path: str | Path,
    meta: VideoMetadata,
    view: View | None = None,
    *,
    seek: str = 'auto',
    seek_threshold: int = 100,
    index: FrameIndex | None = None,
)
```

Keeps one video open and reads frames by index.

Reading forwards only decodes what is in between. Asking for an earlier frame, or one far ahead, means decoding from
a keyframe; `seek` and `index` decide how that is done:

- With `index` (a `FrameIndex`): the reader knows where the keyframes are, so it jumps only when that decodes fewer
  frames than reading on, and never inside a keyframe interval it is already in. After every frame it compares the
  decoder's timestamp with the index; if they ever disagree it warns and falls back to sequential decoding, so a
  wrong frame is never returned silently. This works on variable-frame-rate video too. An index for a different
  file (hash or frame count differs) is ignored with a warning.
- Without an index, `seek="auto"` (default) seeks only if it has been verified for this file: not variable frame rate,
  and the frames returned after seeking are identical to sequential decoding at a few test positions (checked once
  per file per process). Otherwise it decodes sequentially, with a warning.
- `seek="off"`: never seek (the index, if any, is not used).
- `seek="always"`: seek without the pixel check (for tests and for `seek_mismatches`).

`read_many` reads several frames at once in the cheapest order. For training prefer `VideoStream`, which reads each
video front to back. Not thread-safe; use one reader per process or thread.

#### `vidlabel.frames.FrameReader.close`

```python
close() -> None
```

Release the open video file. Safe to call twice; the reader reopens it on the next `read`.

#### `vidlabel.frames.FrameReader.read`

```python
read(index: int) -> np.ndarray
```

RGB frame `index` in displayed orientation, cropped to the view if there is one.

#### `vidlabel.frames.FrameReader.read_many`

```python
read_many(indices: Iterable[int]) -> list[np.ndarray]
```

Frames for `indices`, in the order given. They are read in increasing order so each keyframe interval is
decoded once however the request is ordered; repeated indices are decoded once and copied.

#### `vidlabel.frames.FrameReader.seek_enabled` (property)

Whether this reader will use seeking (without an index, runs the one-off check in "auto" mode).

With `view_id`, shows that view's crop with only that view's annotations, as its pipeline would see them.

### `vidlabel.preview.parse_color`

```python

```

'red', '#ff8800', 'ff8800' or '255,136,0' -> (r, g, b).

### `vidlabel.preview.PreviewStyle`

```python
vidlabel.preview.PreviewStyle(
```

## Probing videos (needs ffprobe)

### `vidlabel.probe.probe_video`

```python
probe_video(path: str | Path, video_id: str | None = None, *, hash: bool = True) -> VideoMetadata
```

Read a video's facts with ffprobe (size, fps as a fraction, frame count, rotation, codec, bit rate) and hash the file
unless `hash=False`. Needs `ffprobe` on the PATH. `video_id` defaults to the file name without extension.

### `vidlabel.probe.file_hash`

```python
file_hash(path: str | Path) -> str
```

`sha256:<hex>` of a file's contents.

### `vidlabel.probe.probe_frame_index`

```python
probe_frame_index(path: str | Path, *, content_hash: str | None = None) -> FrameIndex
```

Read a video's per-frame timestamps and keyframes from its packet table with ffprobe. Nothing is decoded, so it takes
seconds even for long videos. Pass `content_hash` (from the metadata) to record which file the index belongs to.
Raises ValueError if the container has no timestamps (some raw streams), and RuntimeError without ffprobe.

### `vidlabel.probe.reconcile_frame_count`

```python
reconcile_frame_count(meta: VideoMetadata, index: FrameIndex) -> VideoMetadata
```

Make `meta.frame_count` agree with `index`. If the count was only estimated when the video was probed, the index (an
exact count) replaces it; a real disagreement raises ValueError, because one of the two describes a different file.

## Frame cache (`vidlabel.cache`, needs OpenCV)

### `vidlabel.cache.FrameCache`

```python
vidlabel.cache.FrameCache(root: str | Path)
```

Frames saved as `<root>/<video_id>/<frame>.jpg|png`, plus `<root>/cache.json` saying which video file each came from.

Open an existing cache with `FrameCache(root)`; make or extend one with `FrameCache.build(samples, root)`.

#### `vidlabel.cache.FrameCache.build`

```python
build(
    samples,
    root: str | Path,
    *,
    format: str = 'jpg',
    quality: int = 95,
    overwrite: bool = False,
) -> tuple['FrameCache', CacheStats]
```

Decode every frame `samples` (a `FrameSamples`) will use, in order, and save it under `root`.

Frames already cached are kept unless `overwrite=True`. Returns the cache and what was done. Needs OpenCV.

#### `vidlabel.cache.FrameCache.has`

```python
has(video_id: str, frame: int) -> bool
```

#### `vidlabel.cache.FrameCache.read`

```python
read(video_id: str, frame: int) -> np.ndarray
```

The cached frame as an RGB uint8 array (whole frame, displayed orientation). KeyError if it is not cached.

#### `vidlabel.cache.FrameCache.usable`

```python
usable(video_id: str, meta: VideoMetadata) -> bool
```

Whether this cache has frames for the video *as registered*: same file (hash) and same size.

### `vidlabel.cache.CachedReader`

```python
vidlabel.cache.CachedReader(
    cache: FrameCache,
    video_id: str,
    meta: VideoMetadata,
    view: View | None,
    fallback,
)
```

Same interface as `FrameReader` (`read`, `read_many`, `close`), but frames come from a `FrameCache` when it has them
and from the video file otherwise, so a partial cache is fine. Crops to `view` like `FrameReader` does.

#### `vidlabel.cache.CachedReader.close`

```python
close() -> None
```

#### `vidlabel.cache.CachedReader.read`

```python
read(index: int)
```

#### `vidlabel.cache.CachedReader.read_many`

```python
read_many(indices: Iterable[int]) -> list
```

Frames for `indices` in the order given; frames missing from the cache are decoded together, in increasing order.

### `vidlabel.cache.CacheStats`

```python
vidlabel.cache.CacheStats(written: int, skipped: int, bytes: int, seconds: float) -> None
```

What `FrameCache.build` did.

## Masks (`vidlabel.masks`)

### `vidlabel.masks.encode`

```python
encode(mask) -> bytes
```

Encode a boolean (H, W) array: crop to its bounding box, bit-pack the rows, zstd-compress. Lossless.

### `vidlabel.masks.decode`

```python
decode(blob: bytes) -> np.ndarray
```

Full-frame boolean mask (H, W).

### `vidlabel.masks.decode_crop`

```python
decode_crop(blob: bytes) -> tuple[np.ndarray, int, int]
```

Decode only the cropped region: (crop[h, w] bool, y0, x0). Skips allocating the full frame.

### `vidlabel.masks.bbox`

```python
bbox(blob: bytes) -> tuple[int, int, int, int] | None
```

(x0, y0, x1, y1) of the mask, or None if empty.

### `vidlabel.masks.info`

```python
info(blob: bytes) -> dict
```

Read only the header: frame size, crop rectangle. Cheap.

### `vidlabel.masks.place_in_frame`

```python
place_in_frame(mask, x: int, y: int, frame_w: int, frame_h: int) -> np.ndarray
```

Paste a crop-sized mask into an empty full-frame canvas with its top-left at (x, y); parts outside are clipped.

### `vidlabel.masks.resize_nearest`

```python
resize_nearest(mask, h: int, w: int) -> np.ndarray
```

Nearest-neighbour resize of a boolean mask to (h, w).

### `vidlabel.masks.from_coco_rle`

```python
from_coco_rle(rle: dict) -> np.ndarray
```

Decode a COCO RLE dict {'size': [h, w], 'counts': list[int] | str} to a boolean (h, w) mask.

### `vidlabel.masks.to_coco_rle`

```python
to_coco_rle(mask, compressed: bool = False) -> dict
```

A boolean mask as a COCO run-length dict (`counts`, `size`); `compressed=True` gives the compact string form.

## Boxes (`vidlabel.boxes`)

### `vidlabel.boxes.convert_boxes`

```python
convert_boxes(
    boxes,
    src: str = 'xyxy',
    dst: str = 'xyxy',
    *,
    size: tuple[int, int] | None = None,
    src_normalized: bool = False,
    dst_normalized: bool = False,
) -> np.ndarray
```

Convert an (N, 4) array of boxes. `size` is (width, height) of the image they refer to; it is required when
`src_normalized` or `dst_normalized` is set. Returns float32.

### `vidlabel.boxes.rotate_boxes`

```python
rotate_boxes(boxes, rotation: int, stored_size: tuple[int, int]) -> np.ndarray
```

Move (N, 4) `xyxy` boxes from the stored frame to the displayed orientation of a rotated video.

`rotation` is the video's clockwise rotation (0, 90, 180 or 270, as in VideoMetadata.rotation) and `stored_size` is
(width, height) of the stored frame. Annotations in a vidlabel dataset use the displayed orientation, so a source that
drew boxes on the unrotated stored frame needs this before `add_annotations`. x1/y1 stay exclusive.

## Validation

### `vidlabel.validate_dataset`

```python
validate_dataset(path: str | Path, deep: bool = False) -> list[Issue]
```

Validate a whole dataset directory. Never raises for bad data; returns issues.

### `vidlabel.validate.check_annotation_table`

```python
check_annotation_table(
    table: pa.Table,
    *,
    frame_count: int | None = None,
    size: tuple[int, int] | None = None,
    vocab_names: set[str] | None = None,
    views: Mapping[str, View] | None = None,
    video_id: str | None = None,
    deep_masks: bool = False,
) -> list[Issue]
```

Check one annotation table. `size` is (width, height) in display orientation.

`views` maps view_id -> View; rows tagged with a view must lie inside it (region, frame range, allowed labels).

### `vidlabel.Issue` and `vidlabel.ValidationError`

`validate()` returns a list of `Issue(level, code, message, count, sample_ids)`; `level` is `"error"` or `"warning"`. `ValidationError` is raised by writes and by `build` when there are errors; its `.issues` lists them. The codes are listed in the [spec](SPEC.md#validation-codes).

## Spec models (`vidlabel_spec`, also importable from `vidlabel`)

These pydantic models are the contract; unknown fields are rejected (custom data goes in `extra`).

### `VideoMetadata`

Generic facts about one video. Lives in videos/<video_id>/metadata.json.

| field | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `video_id` | `str` | required |  |
| `content_hash` | `str | None` | none | '<algo>:<hex>', e.g. 'sha256:ab12...'. Lets anyone detect a re-encoded or wrong file. |
| `duration_s` | `float | None` | none |  |
| `frame_count` | `int` | required |  |
| `fps` | `Rational` | required |  |
| `timebase` | `Rational | None` | none |  |
| `is_vfr` | `bool` | False |  |
| `width` | `int` | required |  |
| `height` | `int` | required |  |
| `rotation` | `int` | 0 | Clockwise degrees (0, 90, 180, 270) applied to the stored frame to display it upright. 90 and 270 swap width and height. |
| `codec` | `str | None` | none |  |
| `pix_fmt` | `str | None` | none |  |
| `bit_rate` | `int | None` | none | Bits per second as reported by the container/stream. |
| `sources` | `list[VideoSource]` | empty |  |
| `ingested_at` | `datetime.datetime | None` | none |  |
| `extra` | `dict[str, Any]` | empty |  |

### `VideoSource`

One known location of the video file. Several may be listed; paths move, hashes don't.

| field | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `uri` | `str` | required |  |
| `note` | `str | None` | none |  |

### `FrameIndex`

Optional per-frame timing of one video, stored in videos/<video_id>/frame_index.json.

Read from the file's packet table (no decoding), so it is cheap to make. It lets a reader seek by timestamp, including
in variable-frame-rate video, check where a seek really landed, and plan reads so each keyframe interval is decoded once.

`pts` holds one presentation timestamp per frame, in `timebase` ticks, in display order (so `pts[i]` belongs to frame
`i`) and strictly increasing. `keyframes` lists the frame numbers where decoding can start without earlier frames.

| field | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content_hash` | `str | None` | none | Hash of the file this was read from; a different hash means the index is stale. |
| `timebase` | `Rational` | required |  |
| `pts` | `list[int]` | required |  |
| `keyframes` | `list[int]` | empty |  |

### `Rational`

| field | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `num` | `int` | required |  |
| `den` | `int` | required |  |

### `Region`

| field | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | `int` | required |  |
| `y` | `int` | required |  |
| `width` | `int` | required |  |
| `height` | `int` | required |  |

### `View`

A named crop and/or time range of a video. No new video is made; annotations stay in source coordinates.

`region` is in the video's displayed orientation. If the crop is resized before it reaches a pipeline, give
`output_size` (width, height) so coordinates can be converted back. `allowed_labels` optionally limits which
labels may be used in this view (e.g. a caption strip that only allows caption labels).

| field | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `view_id` | `str` | required |  |
| `video_id` | `str` | required |  |
| `name` | `str | None` | none |  |
| `region` | `Region | None` | none |  |
| `output_size` | `tuple[int, int] | None` | none | (width, height) the region is resized to when shown to a pipeline. Omit if not resized. |
| `frame_range` | `tuple[int, int] | None` | none | Inclusive [first, last] frame. |
| `allowed_labels` | `list[str] | None` | none | If set, annotations in this view may only use these labels. |
| `extra` | `dict[str, Any]` | empty |  |

### `Label`

| field | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | required |  |
| `parent` | `str | None` | none |  |
| `description` | `str | None` | none |  |
| `extra` | `dict[str, Any]` | empty |  |

### `Vocab`

The one shared list of labels.

| field | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `version` | `str` | '0' |  |
| `labels` | `list[Label]` | empty |  |

### `Manifest`

Dataset-level index. Lives in manifest.json.

| field | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec_version` | `str` | '0.5.0' |  |
| `videos` | `list[str]` | empty |  |
| `views` | `list[str]` | empty |  |
| `vocab_version` | `str | None` | none |  |
| `extra` | `dict[str, Any]` | empty |  |

### `Release`

Describes one compiled (training) build. release_id is derived from content, so a training run can pin it.

| field | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `release_id` | `str` | required |  |
| `spec_version` | `str` | required |  |
| `created_at` | `datetime.datetime` | required |  |
| `n_rows` | `int` | required |  |
| `n_videos` | `int` | required |  |
| `row_group_size` | `int` | required |  |
| `files` | `dict[str, str]` | required | file name -> 'sha256:<hex>' |
| `extra` | `dict[str, Any]` | empty | Build filters etc. |
